To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the proposed extended TAM model could be used for predicting user acceptance of electronic shopping on the Web; (ii) perceived ease of use (PEO) is a significant factor in determining user acceptance; (iii) user satisfaction with the WWW is a significant factor that influences user acceptance; and (iv) the proposed model could also be used for predicting consumer willingness to shop electronically.

individual attitudes toward electronic-shopping (e-shooping) are strongly and positively related to user acceptance, and that perceived ease of using trading online, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of using the Web, perceived usefulness, user satisfaction with Internet/World Wide Web, perceptions of information, perceptions of service, and perceptions of system are all significant determinants of individual attitudes toward e-shooping.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of user acceptance of e-commerce.
the prediction of user acceptance of e-commerce on the Web.
the development of an extended model of consumer acceptance of e-shopping based on the TRA and the TAM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model is a good model to predict consumer willingness of e-shopping.
the proposed model can be used to predict the willingness of consumers to shop on the Internet.
this study has provided a theoretical framework for predicting the acceptance of e-shopping.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an extended model to explain consumer acceptance of e-shopping.
the results of our study show that the extended TAM model is an appropriate framework for predicting consumer acceptance of e-shopping.
we have proposed and tested a model for predicting consumer acceptance of e-shopping based on the theory and empirical evidence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the model is a useful predictor of user acceptance of e-shoppings on the Web.
we can predict user acceptance of e-commerce by looking at user attitudes, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and user satisfaction with the internet/WWW.
the technology acceptance model and the theory of reasoned actions are both useful in understanding the acceptance of e-shopping.
